rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Cards 4 Scoring 5 Dynamic Market Variant Overview Manage the market over 6 rounds to hold the most valuable vegetables at end game Turn Form the market by placing X+1 cards, where X is the number of players. Each player takes a turn taking a card into their hand. The card not taken will adjust the market values. The price of each vegetable shown on the leftover card is increased. Cards The cards show certain vegetables on them, if you hold these vegetables, you gain their worth at end game If a card isn't chosen, the vegetables on it increase in value by the number shown (e.g. 2 carrots and 1 corn will cause corn to go up 1 step and carrots to go up 2) Watch out, if a vegetable reaches the top value, it loops back around to 0 for its next change Scoring At the end of the 6th round, see where the vegetable values are at, then multiply each by the amount of that vegetable you hold, do the same with all the vegetable values to give you your final score, highest score wins Dynamic Market Variant The dynamic market side of the cards is used when playing with this variant. The difference is that to increase the price from 3 to 5 you will need two of the same symbols to be on the leftover card. If there is only one, the vegetable price stays at 3. If there are 3 of the same vegetables on the leftover card, the vegetable price would jump from 3 to 0.

[Rating: 1/10] A fantastically terrible "game." You are able to influence the markets once per game when you are next to last in turn order. Otherwise, you take a card and hope for the best. In our game, one player chose the first card available in every draw and she tied for first. So playing blind earns you as many points as "strategizing." This game is awful.

[Rating: 2/10] Yes, it's a filler, but a bad one: no fun, no theme, no challenge. Wouldn't have been a hit even 30 years ago.

[Rating: 2/10] No interest. It's like they extracted a part of a bigger game... Boring and nothing new.

[Rating: 3/10] Annoyed with myself for picking this up. I've stumbled into yet another game where you may need to calculate out whether you want to forego a share in something in order to increase the value of what you already have, and it may be a wash.  Even in a two-player game, early moves are completely meaningless. It feels ridiculous to even be asked to choose a move to make.  Like others, I found attractive the notion that whatever item doesn't get drafted, affects the game state in some way. [Rating: 3/10] I cannot believe this was actually made.  There are so few decisions to make.  I don't have any need for a 3 minute game.

[Rating: 3/10] There are more interesting and deeper small card games out there. Felt short and lucky.

[Rating: 3/10] Short and simple rules, and relatively harmless. That's about the only good things I can say about this game. I have played this game with a bunch of different people and not one of us liked it. The game is random, gives a player pretty much no agency, and is way too short to make any strategy meaningful. A total waste of time, but at least that waste is only 5 or 10 minutes.   Forget the people who compare this game to Wildlife Safari. That game is great, fun, mean, and gives players lots of agency. Any comparison to  Wildlife Safari is shallow. That game is great. This one is not.
